For a buyer the practical points are the form bought, the basis a result is reported on, where the cauliflower came from and the laboratory’s reporting limit. Testing finds contamination but does not remove it.

<div class="hmi-analyte-explorer" id="hmi-occurrence-cauliflower" data-analyte-explorer data-compact-intro="true" data-source-summaries="true"><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" data-explorer-context><summary data-open-context aria-haspopup="dialog" aria-controls="hmi-occurrence-cauliflower-drawer">Comparison methods and scope</summary><div data-explorer-context-content>

<p>Each row is one statistic a source reports for one form of cauliflower, group and metal; percentiles, ranges and maxima reported for the same samples as a mean or median are shown on that row. Different forms and preparation states are kept apart, and dry-weight results never share a reference with as-sold or fresh-weight results. Ratings place a result against an HMI reference built from monitoring results and ordinary-setting medians for the same form and basis. Same-study contrasts compare a contaminated or treated site with its control, targeted with random sampling, a prepared form with the unprocessed one, or one group of a study with the median of its other groups. Held rows failed a check against their own source and are shown but not compared.</p>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="which-types-of-cauliflower-have-the-lowest-levels" data-anchor="which-types-of-cauliflower-have-the-lowest-levels" data-question="Which types of cauliflower have the lowest levels?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Which types of cauliflower have the lowest levels?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

For cadmium, the HMI reference median was lowest for cauliflower, cooked (11 µg/kg) and highest for cauliflower, as sold (99 µg/kg); forms differ in water content, so this compares foods as sold or eaten, not uptake.<sup class="cite">[[sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">U.S. Food and Drug <details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="which-regions-report-the-lowest-levels-in-cauliflower" data-anchor="which-regions-report-the-lowest-levels-in-cauliflower" data-question="Which regions report the lowest levels in cauliflower?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Which regions report the lowest levels in cauliflower?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Among GEMS/Food reporting regions, cauliflower, as sold had the lowest cadmium subgroup median in EURO (4.2 µg/kg) and the highest in PAHO (9.5 µg/kg); reporting regions are markets, not growing areas.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="how-much-of-the-arsenic-in-cauliflower-is-inorganic" data-anchor="how-much-of-the-arsenic-in-cauliflower-is-inorganic" data-question="How much of the arsenic in cauliflower is inorganic?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>How much of the arsenic in cauliflower is inorganic?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Inorganic arsenic, the more toxic form, was measured in 6 results from 3 sources, far fewer than total arsenic.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/laizu2007-dhaka-vegetables-arsenic-speciation|15]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Laizu J · 2007</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/laizu2007-dhaka-vegetables-arsenic-speciation">Speciation of arsenic in vegetables and their correlation with inorganic phosphate level</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Bangladesh Journal of Pharmacology 2007; 2: 88-94</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/laizu2007-dhaka-vegetables-arsenic-speciation">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/fera2015-uk-tds-metals|16]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Baxter M, Brereton N · 2015</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fera2015-uk-tds-metals">Total Diet Study of metals and other elements in food</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Food and Environment Research Agency report for the UK Food Standards Agency, Fera report 15/06, project FS102081</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fera2015-uk-tds-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Laizu 2007 reported inorganic arsenic at 400 µg/kg (mean ± 500 SD) in cauliflower, as sold from fruiting vegetables, local market, Dhaka.<sup class="cite">[[sources/laizu2007-dhaka-vegetables-arsenic-speciation|15]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Laizu J · 2007</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/laizu2007-dhaka-vegetables-arsenic-speciation">Speciation of arsenic in vegetables and their correlation with inorganic phosphate level</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Bangladesh Journal of Pharmacology 2007;
